Dear Counsel,

Thank you for sending the Seller’s initial draft. Buyer has reviewed and has the following initial comments.

1. Purchase Price. Buyer cannot agree to USD 45,000,000 on the current draft and diligence posture. Please revise the purchase price to USD 35,000,000.

2. Closing. Please revise closing to occur within 45 days after signing, subject to completion of Buyer’s confirmatory diligence, required approvals, and satisfaction of customary closing conditions.

3. Representations. The single financial-statement representation is insufficient. Please expand the Seller representations to include customary matters for a share purchase, including authority, title to shares, no conflicts, compliance with law, absence of undisclosed liabilities, taxes, material contracts, litigation, employees/benefits, intellectual property, data/privacy, environmental matters, and no material adverse change.

4. Indemnity / Escrow. Please add customary survival and indemnification provisions, including an escrow or holdback equal to 10% of the purchase price for 18 months, with basket, cap, and exceptions to be discussed. Fundamental representations and fraud should not be subject to the general cap.

5. Closing Conditions. Please add a condition that there has been no material adverse change between signing and closing.

6. Confidentiality. Please add standard carve-outs for disclosures to representatives, financing sources, and as required by law or to enforce rights under the agreement.

We look forward to receiving a revised draft.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,000,000 for the Shares, payable in immediately available funds at Closing, subject only to the express adjustments, if any, set forth in this Agreement.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur on the date that is 30 days after signing, or such other date as the parties may agree in writing, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the closing conditions expressly set forth in this Agreement and receipt of any required governmental approvals. For the avoidance of doubt, Buyer’s confirmatory diligence shall be completed prior to signing and shall not constitute a separate condition to Closing unless expressly agreed by Seller in writing.

3. Representations of Seller. Seller represents and warrants to Buyer as follows: (a) Seller has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (b) Seller owns the Shares free and clear of liens other than restrictions under applicable securities laws and liens arising through Buyer; (c) execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by Seller do not conflict with Seller’s organizational documents or any material contract binding on Seller; (d) to Seller’s knowledge, the Company is in material compliance with applicable laws; (e) the financial statements delivered to Buyer were prepared in good faith from the Company’s books and records and fairly present in all material respects the financial position of the Company as of the dates indicated; (f) to Seller’s knowledge, the Company has no undisclosed liabilities required by applicable accounting principles to be reflected on the financial statements, except liabilities incurred in the ordinary course of business since the date of the most recent balance sheet; (g) the Company has filed material tax returns required to be filed and paid material taxes due, except those being contested in good faith; (h) Seller has made available to Buyer copies of material contracts requested by Buyer; (i) to Seller’s knowledge, there is no material litigation pending against the Company; (j) to Seller’s knowledge, the Company is in material compliance with applicable employment and benefits laws; (k) to Seller’s knowledge, the Company owns or has the right to use the intellectual property material to its business; (l) to Seller’s knowledge, the Company is in material compliance with applicable data privacy and security laws; (m) to Seller’s knowledge, the Company is in material compliance with applicable environmental laws; and (n) since the date of the most recent financial statements made available to Buyer, there has been no material adverse change in the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition or results of operations of the Company, taken as a whole, other than changes resulting from general economic, market, industry, legal or geopolitical conditions or other matters not disproportionately affecting the Company.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement are confidential; provided that a party may disclose such terms (a) to its affiliates, representatives, legal counsel, accountants, tax advisors, financing sources and other professional advisors who are informed of the confidential nature of the information, (b) as required by applicable law, regulation, court order or securities exchange rule, and (c) as necessary to enforce its rights or perform its obligations under this Agreement.

5. Closing Conditions. The obligations of Buyer and Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement are subject to: (a) the accuracy of the other party’s representations and warranties in all material respects as of Closing, except for representations qualified by materiality, which shall be accurate in all respects; (b) performance in all material respects by the other party of its covenants required to be performed prior to Closing; (c) receipt of required governmental approvals; and (d) no law or order prohibiting the Closing. Buyer’s obligation to close is further subject to the absence of a material adverse change with respect to the Company between signing and Closing, subject to customary exclusions for general economic, market, industry, legal or geopolitical conditions or other matters not disproportionately affecting the Company.

6. Survival; Indemnification; Escrow. The representations and warranties shall survive Closing for 12 months, except that fundamental representations regarding authority and title to the Shares and claims based on fraud shall survive for the applicable statute of limitations. Seller shall indemnify Buyer for losses arising from breaches of Seller’s representations, warranties and covenants, subject to a deductible basket equal to 1.0% of the Purchase Price and an aggregate cap equal to 7.5% of the Purchase Price for non-fundamental representations. Claims for breach of fundamental representations and fraud shall not be subject to the foregoing deductible or general cap, but Seller’s aggregate liability shall not exceed the Purchase Price except in the case of actual fraud. At Closing, 5.0% of the Purchase Price shall be deposited into escrow for 12 months as Buyer’s sole source of recovery for non-fundamental representation claims, except in the case of fraud.

receiver.requested_changes: Buyer requests the following revisions: (1) Purchase Price reduced to USD 39,000,000; alternatively, Buyer can discuss USD 40,000,000 if Seller accepts the enhanced escrow/cap/survival package below. (2) Closing conditionality to include completion of Buyer’s confirmatory diligence to Buyer’s reasonable satisfaction, or at minimum no material adverse findings in confirmatory diligence before Closing. (3) Seller representations to be expanded and de-qualified in key areas: financial statements, no undisclosed liabilities, taxes, material contracts, compliance with laws, litigation, employment/benefits, IP, privacy/security, environmental, and absence of changes. (4) Survival for general representations increased to 18 months; tax, employment/benefits, privacy/security, and environmental reps to survive 36 months; fundamental reps and fraud to survive through the applicable statute of limitations. (5) Escrow increased to 10% of the Purchase Price for 18 months. (6) Basket to be 0.5% of Purchase Price and structured as a tipping basket, not a deductible. (7) Cap for non-fundamental representations increased to 15% of Purchase Price. (8) Escrow not to be Buyer’s sole source of recovery for breaches of covenants, special indemnities, fundamental representations, purchase price adjustment matters, equitable relief, or fraud. (9) Fraud carve-out to include intentional misrepresentation and deliberate concealment, and liability for fraud not capped. (10) Add ordinary-course covenant between signing and Closing and a no-MAC closing condition.
receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft. Seller’s movement is appreciated, and the expanded representation and indemnity framework is a constructive step. That said, the current draft still leaves Buyer bearing a disproportionate amount of post-Closing and diligence risk, particularly given the breadth of the knowledge/materiality qualifiers, the absence of a meaningful diligence condition, and the limited escrow/cap package.

Buyer is prepared to continue constructively on the following basis:

1. Purchase Price. Buyer’s revised proposal is USD 39,000,000. If Seller is prepared to accept the enhanced recourse package outlined below, Buyer would consider discussing USD 40,000,000.

2. Diligence / Closing Condition. Buyer cannot accept language providing that confirmatory diligence is completed solely before signing with no continuing protection. Please revise to include a condition that Buyer’s confirmatory diligence has been completed to Buyer’s reasonable satisfaction, or at minimum that no material adverse findings arise before Closing.

3. Representations. The added representations are helpful, but many are overly qualified. Please remove or narrow knowledge and materiality qualifiers for core areas, including financial statements, undisclosed liabilities, taxes, material contracts, legal compliance, litigation, employment/benefits, IP, privacy/security, environmental matters, and absence of changes.

4. Survival. General representations should survive for 18 months. Tax, employment/benefits, privacy/security, and environmental representations should survive for 36 months. Fundamental representations and fraud should survive for the applicable statute of limitations.

5. Escrow / Basket / Cap. Buyer proposes a 10% escrow for 18 months, a 0.5% tipping basket, and a 15% cap for non-fundamental representation claims. The escrow should not be Buyer’s sole source of recovery for covenants, special indemnities, fundamental representations, purchase price adjustment matters, equitable relief, or fraud.

6. Fraud. The fraud carve-out should expressly include intentional misrepresentation and deliberate concealment, with no cap on liability for fraud.

7. Interim Covenants / No MAC. Please add customary ordinary-course operating covenants between signing and Closing and a no-MAC closing condition.

We think the above provides a balanced path to signing: a lower headline price reflecting Seller’s proposed limited recourse, or a modestly higher price if Seller is willing to stand behind the business with customary protections.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP
